title: Contract revision, irreversible forgetting, and revision debt
question: After a scientific contract has compressed model worlds into a state, can a later required state be recovered from that stored state alone, and if not, what is the minimum exact auxiliary information required?

objects.meaning: Partition stored under an earlier scientific contract.
World-level required partition under a later or joint contract.
Number of revised-state blocks intersecting old block B.
Maximum split multiplicity and exact minimum auxiliary alphabet size.
log2 K_rev; idealized worst-case local revision burden.
log2(|P join Q|/|P|); global average split burden.

results.claim: The revised state factors through the old state label iff every old-state block lies inside one revised-state block.
results.claim_ceiling: Finite deterministic factorization on one common carrier.

results.claim: The exact minimum auxiliary alphabet size for revision is max_B r_B(P,Q).
results.claim_ceiling: Zero-error finite auxiliary labels; not Shannon rate or empirical sampling cost.

results.claim: Revision debt is monotone upward under refinement of the revised required partition and monotone downward under refinement of the retained old partition.
Global average refinement debt is bounded above by worst-case revision debt.
For every m>=1 and epsilon>0, finite partitions exist with m bits of worst-case revision debt and average refinement debt below epsilon.
results.claim_ceiling: Existence construction; no claim about empirical frequency.

composition.world_level_stage: Compute Q for the revised/joint contract using the CREST common-lift construction.
composition.revision_stage: Apply TU-1 to test whether Q factors through stored P and, if not, quantify exact auxiliary revision requirements.
composition.prohibited_shortcut: Do not assume an old scientifically adequate state remains revisable after the contract changes.

prior_art_firewall: Closure-operator joint-state existence/order independence remains CREST-J1 and classical fixed-point substrate.
TU-1B is closely related to finite zero-error coding / side-information partition problems.
Do not claim standalone information-theory novelty without a dedicated prior-art audit.
open_extensions: Carrier-changing revision through a declared replacement relation or faithful common lift.
Probabilistic/expected revision cost under a declared world distribution.
Approximate revision under tolerance-qualified state equivalence.
Empirical revision cost when auxiliary labels must be measured through a failure-prone observation contract.
